stories.body: Canada will impose retaliatory tariffs “dollar for dollar” after last-minute US-Canada trade negotiations collapsed and new 50% US tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian goods took effect. Prime Minister Mark Carney said Washington's revised terms were unfair and unreliable, while US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer blamed Canada for introducing new demands and abandoning earlier commitments. The measures affect products including dairy, wine, clothing, cement and hockey equipment, adding to existing US tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminium, autos and lumber.
stories.headline: Canada vows to match new US tariffs after trade talks collapse

stories.body: At least 16 people were killed and about 130 injured, including 23 children, after Russian drones struck a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, Ukrainian officials said. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack came in two waves, with the second drone hitting the burning building about half an hour later and targeting emergency responders. Nine people, including two children, were still reported missing in the rubble as rescue teams expanded their search. The attack prompted renewed calls from Ukraine and EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas for stronger pressure on Russia.
stories.headline: Russian double drone strike on Kryvyi Rih shopping centre kills at least 16

stories.body: Israel's opening of tenders for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem has drawn condemnation from the UN, European countries and Canada. Critics say construction there would split the occupied West Bank between north and south, isolate East Jerusalem and make a contiguous Palestinian state far more difficult to establish. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the project an existential threat to a two-state solution, while Israel's government has continued to advance settlement expansion despite longstanding international objections.
stories.headline: International opposition grows to Israel's E1 West Bank settlement project

stories.body: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said it was time to end the months-long war with the United States from what he described as a position of strength, while President Donald Trump said Tehran was not ready to make the right deal. Iranian and Omani foreign ministers discussed conditions for restarting talks as shipping disruptions continued in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has kept traffic partly restricted and the US has reportedly protected tanker convoys. Washington is also preparing a new sanctions campaign against Iran.
stories.headline: US and Iran remain at odds over terms to end war as Hormuz pressure grows

stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 2,500 people and is spreading faster than the response, according to the UN's senior Ebola coordinator. More than half of the deaths have occurred in the past 20 days, while the outbreak has spread across an area larger than France. Authorities are preparing to use 20,000 doses of the Ervebo vaccine in a trial against the Bundibugyo strain now circulating, for which no proven vaccine or treatment exists, alongside doses for frontline health workers.
stories.headline: UN warns Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is growing exponentially

stories.body: A federal judge in Manhattan has struck down the Trump administration's suspension of immigrant visas for applicants from 75 countries, ruling that Secretary of State Marco Rubio exceeded his legal authority. Judge Jeannette Vargas called the policy patently unlawful and said it conflicted with immigration law governing consular visa decisions. The suspension, introduced in January, affected applicants from countries across Latin America, Africa, the Middle East, South Asia, the Balkans and the Caribbean.
stories.headline: Federal judge strikes down Trump's immigrant visa suspension affecting 75 countries

stories.body: The federal government will reduce water deliveries from the Colorado River to Arizona, California and Nevada beginning in 2027 as the river's supply continues to decline. The cuts will require the three states to curb their use of a water source that supports major cities, agriculture and industry across the US Southwest.
stories.headline: Federal government will cut Colorado River water deliveries to Arizona, California and Nevada from 2027

stories.body: President Donald Trump held a rally in Myrtle Beach to support Senator Darline Graham before her South Carolina Republican runoff against Representative Ralph Norman, urging voters to treat the contest as if he were on the ballot. Graham, who is seeking to retain the seat formerly held by her late brother Lindsey Graham, has faced criticism after saying at a debate that national security was not her strength. The unusually high-profile intervention in a safely Republican state has prompted some party operatives to question why Trump has offered less direct help to candidates in more competitive midterm races.
stories.headline: Trump campaigns for Darline Graham in South Carolina amid Republican doubts over his midterm focus

stories.body: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers has called for a one-year moratorium on new data centres in the state while officials establish stronger approval rules. Rogers said the pause should protect local control, prevent electricity-price increases, safeguard water supplies and stop pay-to-play arrangements. The position marks a shift for Rogers and highlights how data-centre development has become a growing political issue as communities raise concerns about power demand, water use and utility bills.
stories.headline: Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers calls for one-year Michigan data centre moratorium

stories.body: Spain has appointed Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres to coordinate the ministries involved in the migration emergency in Ceuta, following the mass irregular arrivals from Morocco on 30 and 31 July. Torres, a former president of the Canary Islands with experience managing migration crises, is expected to oversee departments including interior, foreign affairs, defence, migration, health, and youth and children.
stories.headline: Spain appoints cabinet coordinator for continuing Ceuta migration crisis

stories.body: Hundreds of migrants have returned to camp on Ceuta's El Trampolín beach after authorities moved more than 1,200 people to newly opened temporary reception sites. Many migrants fear deportation, do not understand where they should go, or say the available facilities lack adequate space and services. Aid groups warn that thousands remain vulnerable, including women, children and sick people, while the government says it has opened 1,800 places and plans to expand capacity to 5,000.
stories.headline: Migrants continue sleeping outdoors in Ceuta as resettlement efforts proceed slowly

stories.body: Moroccan Justice Minister Abdellatif Ouahbi has renewed Rabat's claim that Ceuta and Melilla are a historic and geographic right of Morocco, calling for dialogue with Spain over their future. Spain's foreign ministry rejected the remarks through diplomatic channels, saying both cities are Spanish territory, part of the European Union and protected by internationally recognised Spanish sovereignty. The exchange comes amid the continuing migration emergency in Ceuta.
stories.headline: Morocco renews claim that Ceuta and Melilla are Moroccan territory amid migration crisis

stories.body: A wildfire believed to have been started by lightning near Segorbe in Castellón has forced the evacuation of about 1,000 residents of nearby Gátova and burned roughly 423 hectares, including land around the Sierra Calderona natural park. Officials said shifting winds, high temperatures, dry terrain and difficult access complicated firefighting, though conditions were expected to improve overnight. Around 280 personnel, aerial resources and military emergency support were deployed as two active fronts remained.
stories.headline: Wildfire near Segorbe forces evacuation of around 1,000 people in Valencia region

stories.body: Torrential rain has flooded roads and disrupted rail services on the Costa Daurada after more than 100 litres per square metre fell in parts of Baix Penedès and Tarragonès, with some locations receiving close to 200 litres in only a few hours. The N-340 was closed between El Vendrell and Torredembarra, while flooding near Sant Vicenç de Calders halted several Rodalies lines. Emergency services received hundreds of weather-related calls, and Civil Protection maintained its flood alert as further heavy storms were forecast for southern Catalonia.
stories.headline: Torrential rain disrupts roads and rail services on Catalonia's Costa Daurada

stories.body: The far-right Save Europe Act movement plans to display a giant banner reading “Remigration saves Europe” in Barcelona's Plaça de Sant Jaume, prompting opposition from anti-fascist groups and political parties. The movement advocates a European ban on non-Western immigration, restrictions on family reunification and faster removals of undocumented migrants, framing its campaign as a defence of European identity. The European Commission rejected its proposed citizens' initiative in July on the grounds that it conflicted with fundamental rights and EU values.
stories.headline: Far-right Save Europe Act demonstration in Barcelona draws political and anti-fascist opposition

stories.body: Workers at Barcelona's CAP Pare Claret primary-care centre say a cooling-system failure since May has left consultation rooms without air conditioning through the summer, with indoor temperatures exceeding 30C and reported heat sensations reaching 37C. Staff say patients and workers have suffered dizziness and fainting, and that fans have provided inadequate relief. The Catalan Health Institute says it has installed 18 portable air-conditioning units and is working on the fault, but staff have been told a full repair may not come until October.
stories.headline: Barcelona clinic staff say they have endured months without functioning air conditioning
